rec.no_description: No description yet. Edit the record or let the AI assistant draft one.
rec.no_items_body: Add a copy so patrons can find and borrow this title.

delete_blocked.one: {count} copy is on loan — check it in before deleting the record.
delete_blocked.other: {count} copies are on loan — check them in before deleting the record.

delete_text.other: “{title}” and its {count} items will be withdrawn from the catalogue. The change is recorded in the audit log.

rec.not_found_body: It may have been deleted or merged into another record.

ai.title: AI cataloguing
ai.intro_record: Suggests subject headings, a Dewey class, the audience and a summary from this record and similar titles. Nothing changes until you accept a suggestion.
ai.nothing: No new suggestions — this record already looks complete.

items.title: Items
items.subtitle: Every physical copy of this title. Select rows for bulk changes; press E on a row to edit it in place.
items.barcode_hint: Scan or type the barcode. Leave it blank to generate one.
items.delete_text: The copy is removed from the catalogue. Loan history is kept for reports.
items.protected_hint: Items on loan, in transit or on the hold shelf are skipped.
items.location_clear_hint: Leave empty to clear the shelf location.

bulk_type_title.one: Change the item type of {count} item
bulk_type_title.other: Change the item type of {count} items

bulk_location_title.one: Set the shelf location of {count} item
bulk_location_title.other: Set the shelf location of {count} items

bulk_delete_text.one: The selected copy is removed from the catalogue.
bulk_delete_text.other: The selected copies are removed from the catalogue.

bulk_delete_protected.one: {count} of them is on loan or on the hold shelf and will be kept.
bulk_delete_protected.other: {count} of them are on loan or on the hold shelf and will be kept.

holds.title: Holds
holds.subtitle: Patrons waiting for this title, in queue order.
holds.no_permission: You do not have permission to manage holds.
holds.cancel_text: {name} will be told that the hold was cancelled.
holds.empty_body: Holds placed on this title will appear here in queue order.
holds.patron_hint: Type at least two letters and choose the patron, or enter a card number.
holds.placed_toast: Hold placed — position {position} in the queue

marc.origin_stored: Stored MARC record (as imported or last edited).
marc.origin_generated: Generated from the catalogue fields — no MARC record is stored yet.
marc.title: MARC editor
marc.discard_text: Your unsaved edits will be lost and the stored record reloaded.
marc.generated_notice: This record has no stored MARC yet, so one was generated from its catalogue fields. Saving stores it.
marc.holdings_notice: {n} holdings fields (952) are hidden here — items are never changed by this editor.
marc.leader_hint: 24 positions · 05 status · 06 type · 07 level · 09 coding (a = Unicode)
marc.help_idle: Focus a field to see its MARC 21 meaning, indicators and subfields.
marc.blank_hint: Blank indicators may be typed as space, # or _. Enter moves to the next box.
marc.not_in_dict: Not in the built-in dictionary (a local or rarely used field).
marc.type_tag: Type a three-digit tag — suggestions appear as you type.
marc.err_code: {tag}: subfield code “{code}” is not a letter or digit
marc.no_problems: No problems found. A 245 field with $a is required.

unreadable.one: {n} line could not be read — see Checks
unreadable.other: {n} lines could not be read — see Checks

marc.text_label: MarcEdit mnemonic — one field per line: =245  10$aTitle
marc.xml_hint: Paste a MARCXML record to replace this one.
marc.text_hint: Blanks are shown as \ in indicators and fixed fields; a literal $ is written {dollar}.
marc.switch_back: Switch back to Fields to see checks and help.
marc.items_untouched: Items are not affected. Field 005 is updated automatically.

history.title: History
history.subtitle: Every change to this record and its items, newest first.
history.empty_body: Changes made from now on appear here.
history.biblio_copycat_import: {who} imported the record by copy cataloguing

item_batch_modify.one: {who} changed {n} item in a batch edit ({fields})
item_batch_modify.other: {who} changed {n} items in a batch edit ({fields})

dupes.title: Possible duplicates
dupes.subtitle: Records with the same ISBN or a near-identical title. Compare them before adding copies.
dupes.none_body: No other record shares this ISBN or title.
dupes.merge_hint: Highlighted rows differ. Keep the more complete record, add any missing copies to it, then delete the other one.

edit.subtitle_new: Scan an ISBN to fill in the details, then review the suggestions alongside. Only the title is required.
edit.subtitle_edit: Changes are saved to the catalogue record and its MARC.
edit.sec_identify_desc: Scanning the ISBN fetches the details and checks for duplicates.
edit.isbn_help: Scan or type the ISBN and press Enter to fetch the details.
edit.sec_title_desc: As it appears on the title page.
edit.authors_help: Pick an authorised name from the list, or press Enter to add it as typed (Surname, Forename).
edit.sec_pub_desc: Imprint details from the title page verso.
edit.sec_content_desc: What the item is about and who it is for. Drives search, facets and recommendations.
edit.subjects_help: Pick authorised headings from the list; use “ -- ” between subdivisions.
edit.sec_cover_desc: Optional. Covers are fetched by ISBN automatically.
edit.cover_help: A link to a cover image. You can also upload one on the record page.
edit.keys_hint: Ctrl+S saves · Enter in the ISBN field looks it up · ; adds a heading as typed
edit.isbn_first: Enter or scan an ISBN first.
edit.isbn_invalid: This ISBN's check digit is wrong — look for a typing error.
edit.year_invalid: Enter a year no later than next year.
edit.cover_invalid: Use a web address that starts with http:// or https://.

assist.title: Cataloguing assistant
assist.dupes_idle: Type a title or scan an ISBN to check the catalogue for duplicates.
assist.dupes_hint: If it is the same edition, add a copy to the existing record instead.
assist.isbn_idle: Look up an ISBN to see what Open Library knows about it. You choose what to keep.
assist.isbn_exists: This ISBN is already in the catalogue.
assist.isbn_not_found: Nothing was found online for this ISBN. Search other library catalogues, or catalogue it by hand.
assist.isbn_found: Found in {source}. Accept the fields you want to keep.
assist.isbn_same: Everything matches what you have entered.
assist.ai_idle: Suggests subjects, a Dewey class, the audience and a summary once there is a title.

acq.title: Acquisitions
acq.subtitle: Budgets, vendors and purchase orders — from draft to delivered — with demand signals from the hold queue.
acq.vendors_sub: Suppliers you order from, with your negotiated discount.
acq.overspent: Overspent — raise the allocation or cancel an order.
acq.no_budgets_body: Create a budget for each fund you spend from, then place orders against it.
acq.allocation_hint: At least {amount}, the amount already committed.
acq.search_placeholder: Title, ISBN, order number or note…
acq.no_orders_body: Clear the filters, or start a new purchase order.
acq.bulk_place_none: None of the selected orders is a draft.
acq.bulk_cancel_none: None of the selected orders can be cancelled.
acq.bulk_cancel_text: The money is released back to each order's budget. Received orders are not affected.
acq.draft_hint: This draft reserves money in its budget but has not been sent to the vendor. Place it when you are ready.
acq.draft_from_suggestion: Created when a patron's purchase suggestion was accepted. Check the vendor and price, then place it.
acq.cancel_text: “{title}” ({amount}) will be cancelled and the money released back to the {budget} budget.
acq.adds_to_record: Copies are added to record {no} when they arrive.
acq.draft_explain: “Save as draft” reserves the money without sending the order; place it when you are ready.
acq.total_over: more than the {remaining} left in this budget
acq.need_vendor: Add a vendor before placing orders.
acq.need_budget: Create a budget before placing orders.

receive_text.one: Receive {count} copy of “{title}” from {vendor}. A new item and barcode is created; the record is matched by ISBN or created.
receive_text.other: Receive {count} copies of “{title}” from {vendor}. One item with a new barcode is created per copy; the record is matched by ISBN or created.

receive_text_record.one: Receive {count} copy of “{title}” from {vendor}. A new item and barcode is added to the record.
receive_text_record.other: Receive {count} copies of “{title}” from {vendor}. One item with a new barcode is added to the record per copy.

acq.no_vendors_body: Add the suppliers you order from.
acq.ai_sub: Titles whose hold queues outstrip available copies
acq.ai_note: Suggests enough copies to bring each queue down to about two holds per copy.
acq.ai_none_body: No title has more holds than its copies can serve right now.

patron_pending.one: {count} patron purchase suggestion is waiting for review.
patron_pending.other: {count} patron purchase suggestions are waiting for review.

auth.title: Authorities
auth.subtitle: Authorised names, subjects and series with their see-from and see-also references. Record headings link to them automatically.
auth.no_match_body: Try part of the heading, or clear the filters.
auth.empty_body: Create one, import MARC authority records, or generate them from your catalogue's headings (Tools).
auth.pick_body: Select a heading on the left to see its references and the records that use it.
auth.read_only: You can view authorities but not change them.
auth.heading: Authorised heading
auth.heading_help: Use “ -- ” between subdivisions, e.g. World War, 1939-1945 -- Fiction.
auth.keep_variant: If I change the heading, keep the current form as a see-from variant
auth.variants_help: Press Enter or ; after each form. Records that use a variant are rewritten to the authorised heading.
auth.see_also_help: Choose the relationship, then type a heading (suggestions come from your authorities).
auth.no_linked: No records use this heading yet.
auth.in_use_merge: This heading is in use — merge it into another authority instead of deleting it.

delete_text.one: “{heading}” and its {n} variant will be removed.
delete_text.other: “{heading}” and its {n} variants will be removed.

auth.merge_intro: Choose the authority to keep. Only {type} authorities can be chosen. The merged heading becomes a see-from variant so future records still match.
auth.merge_keep_help: Type part of the heading and choose from the list.
auth.merge_choose: Choose the authority to keep from the list.
auth.merge_summary: “{from}” ({from_n} records) will be merged into “{to}” ({to_n} records) and then deleted.
auth.variants_added: Variants added to the kept authority
auth.no_text_changes: No record text changes — only the links move.
auth.unlinked_intro: Headings in your records that no authority controls, most used first. Create an authority, or add the heading as a variant of a close match so the records are corrected automatically.
auth.all_controlled_body: All the names, subjects and series in your records link to an authority.

add_variant_text.one: “{heading}” becomes a see-from variant of “{target}”. {n} record will be rewritten to the authorised form.
add_variant_text.other: “{heading}” becomes a see-from variant of “{target}”. {n} records will be rewritten to the authorised form.

auth.gen_intro: Creates a local authority for every heading in your records that is not yet controlled. Useful once, when you start using authority control. Nothing is created until you confirm.
auth.gen_min: Only headings used in at least this many records
auth.gen_need_role: Choose at least one kind of heading.
auth.gen_nothing: Every heading is already controlled — nothing to create.
auth.gen_note: Showing the {n} most used. Types are guessed (organisations become corporate names); review them afterwards.
auth.import_intro: MARC 21 authority records in MARCXML or ISO 2709 (.mrc). Headings 100/110/111/130/150/151/155 become authorities; 4XX become see-from variants and 5XX see-also references. Existing headings are updated, not duplicated.
auth.relink_text: Every record's headings are matched against the authorities again, and see-from variants are rewritten to the authorised form. This is safe to repeat.

labels.title: Labels & cards
labels.subtitle: Spine labels, barcode labels and patron cards on standard label sheets — start part-way through a used sheet.
labels.layouts_sub: Presets for common label sheets, plus your own.
labels.start_help: Or click the first free position on the preview.
labels.split: Split Dewey numbers at the decimal point (823 / .912)
labels.patron_help: Combine any of these; at least one is needed. Up to 5,000 cards per job.
labels.barcodes_placeholder: Scan or paste barcodes, one per line
labels.record_help: Type to search the catalogue, then choose the record.
labels.l_hint: Measure from the top-left corner of the sheet. Print a test sheet with “Print outlines” to check the alignment.
labels.delete_text: “{name}” will be removed. Print jobs that used it are not affected.
labels.sheet_label: First sheet preview — choose the starting label
labels.choose_items: Choose the items to print to see a preview.
labels.choose_patrons: Choose which patrons' cards to print to see a preview.

unencodable.one: {n} value cannot be printed as a barcode (unsupported characters).
unencodable.other: {n} values cannot be printed as a barcode (unsupported characters).

labels.first_sheet_only: The preview shows the first sheet.

lprint.title: Print labels
lprint.hint: In the print dialog choose 100% / actual size and no margins.

missing.one: {count} barcode was not found and is skipped:
missing.other: {count} barcodes were not found and are skipped:

errors.one: {count} value cannot be encoded as Code 128 and prints as text only.
errors.other: {count} values cannot be encoded as Code 128 and print as text only.

batch.subtitle: Change many items at once with a preview of every change, withdraw or delete in bulk, and run a stocktake.
batch.need_barcode: Enter or scan at least one barcode.
batch.need_criterion: Give at least one search criterion.
batch.changes_help: Tick each change you want. Anything left unticked is not touched.
batch.no_match_body: Check the barcodes or widen the search.

apply_text.one: {n} item will be updated. Items whose state changed since the preview are checked again.
apply_text.other: {n} items will be updated. Items whose state changed since the preview are checked again.

batch.delete_empty: Also delete records left with no items (only when nobody is waiting for them)
batch.protected: Items on loan, in transit or waiting on the hold shelf are always protected.
batch.delete_text: The items are removed from the catalogue. This is recorded in the audit log and cannot be undone here.
batch.withdraw_text: The items stay in the catalogue as withdrawn, with their history. This is recorded in the audit log.

inv.mark_seen: Record scanned items as seen today
inv.intro: Scan every item on the shelf (or upload a scanner file), then compare. You will see what is missing, what belongs elsewhere and items whose status is wrong — for example on loan but actually on the shelf.
inv.need_scans: Scan or upload some barcodes first.

cc.subtitle: Search the Library of Congress and other library catalogues, check the MARC record and import it in one step.
cc.author: Author
cc.none_body: Try fewer words, the ISBN, or another catalogue — or catalogue the item by hand.
cc.start_body: Search by title, ISBN or author. Records you already hold are flagged before you import.
cc.already: A record with this ISBN is already in your catalogue.
cc.dup_text: Record {no} already has this ISBN. Import another bibliographic record anyway?
cc.no_targets_body: An administrator can add one under Interoperability › Copy-cataloguing targets.

ser.subtitle: Subscriptions, predicted issues, check-in, late issues and vendor claims.
ser.no_subs_body: Clear the filters, or create a subscription to start predicting issues.
ser.late_intro: Issues become late after their expected date plus the subscription's grace period. Select issues to claim them from their vendors — one letter per vendor.
ser.no_late_body: Every expected issue has arrived on time.
ser.no_claims_body: Claims you send from “Late issues & claims” appear here with their letters.
ser.renewals_intro: Subscriptions ending within 90 days and those that lapsed in the last 30 days.
ser.no_renewals_body: No subscription ends in the next 90 days.

claim_intro.one: Claim {n} issue from {vendors}. The claim is recorded with today's date and the issue is marked claimed.
claim_intro.other: Claim {n} issues from {vendors}. Each claim is recorded with today's date and the issues are marked claimed.

ser.vendor_note_ph: e.g. Please send replacement copies to the Central Library.

open_letters.one: Open the printable claim letter afterwards
open_letters.other: Open the printable claim letters afterwards

ser.renew_predict: Issues are predicted up to the new end date.
ser.predict_intro: Create or refresh predicted issues. Issues already received, claimed, marked missing or added by hand are never changed.
ser.predict_help: Never beyond the subscription's end date.
ser.cancel_text: Cancel the subscription to “{title}”? Future predicted issues that have not been touched are removed; received and claimed issues are kept.
ser.add_irregular: Leave the enumeration blank to continue the numbering pattern.
ser.add_regular: For special issues, supplements or an issue the prediction missed.
ser.keys: Keyboard: ↑ ↓ move · R or Enter receive · C claim · M missing · U undo receipt · Space select
ser.routing_help: Received issues are passed along this list, in order, before going to the shelf.
ser.no_routing: No routing list. Received issues go straight to the shelf.
ser.add_reader: Add a staff member or patron
ser.irregular_empty: Irregular serial: add issues as they are announced.
ser.only_claimable: Only late, missing or claimed issues can be claimed ({list}…)
ser.each_item: Each gets a new item with an automatic barcode.
ser.undo_text_item: {issue} goes back to expected and item {barcode} is deleted. This is only possible if it has never been loaned.
ser.saved_regen: Saved · predictions refreshed ({created} new, {updated} updated, {removed} removed)

sf.need_record: Choose a serial record or create a new one.
sf.grace_help: Late after the expected date plus the grace period
sf.preset_vol_no: Vol. X, No. Y (12 per volume)
sf.preset_vol_no_yearly: Vol. X, No. Y (numbers restart each year)
sf.preset_vol_no_part: Vol. X, No. Y, Pt. Z
sf.levels_help: The innermost level advances every issue; when it passes “roll over after” it resets and the next level out advances. “Yearly” restarts a level each January.
sf.create_items: Create an item (with a barcode) for each received issue
sf.need_start: Enter a start date to see the predictions.
sf.irregular: Irregular serials are not predicted — add each issue by hand when it is announced.
sf.none_in_range: No issues fall between today and the end date.

claims.subtitle: One letter per vendor. Print them, or e-mail the vendor directly.
claims.body: The following issues on our subscriptions with you have not been received. Please supply them, or let us know when they will be dispatched.
claims.subject: Claim for missing issues — {library}
claims.no_email: No e-mail address on file for this vendor — print and post this letter.
claims.not_found: This claim batch does not exist

crs.subtitle: Courses, instructors and short-loan reserve copies. Deactivating a course restores its items.
crs.end_term_text: Deactivate every active course in a term. Items on reserve only for those courses get their normal item type and shelf location back.
crs.end_term_keep: The courses and their reserve lists are kept, ready for next time.
crs.no_terms: No courses have a term set.

activated.one: {n} course activated · {items} item(s) moved to reserve
activated.other: {n} courses activated · {items} item(s) moved to reserve

crs.empty_body: Clear the filters, or create a course.
crs.name: Course name
crs.active_help: Active (reserves applied, visible in the catalogue)

delete_text.one: Delete the course and its {n} reserve? Items return to their normal type and location unless another active course still reserves them.
delete_text.other: Delete the course and its {n} reserves? Items return to their normal type and location unless another active course still reserves them.

crs.scan: Scan or type an item barcode
crs.reserve_type: While on reserve, the item type becomes
crs.find: …or find a title in the catalogue
crs.remove_restores: The item's normal item type and shelf location are restored.
crs.removed_restored: Removed · the item is back to its normal type and location
crs.no_reserves_body: Scan a barcode or find a title above to add it.
